nodes.label: Email Client Compatibility Design (table layout, flat hex, no SVG/box-shadow)
nodes.rationale: Table-based layout (no CSS Grid/Flexbox/gap) and flat hex colors instead of color-mix()/rgba() chosen because near-zero email-client support exists for the modern alternatives (per Mailpit's caniemail-backed check): rgba() has real gaps across Outlook Windows 2007-2019, Yahoo, AOL, WEB.DE, GMX, Apple Mail iOS 11, Orange, and Gmail strips the whole style attribute/<style> block on rgba()'s syntax. box-shadow is dropped everywhere since caniemail shows it unsupported/partial across the majority of the digest's real audience. Unicode glyphs (★, ↗, ③) replace inline <svg> since several clients (Outlook Windows, Gmail, Yahoo, AOL) strip unsupported <svg> elements and any fallback content entirely rather than just ignoring them. The @media stacking technique is the standard responsive-email approach (also used by MJML, Foundation for Emails); Outlook desktop's Word engine is an accepted degradation since deep MSO-conditional-comment hackery isn't worth it for a single-operator daily digest.
nodes.norm_label: email client compatibility design (table layout, flat hex, no svg/box-shadow)

nodes.label: Reserved Search (v2) Placeholder
nodes.rationale: Inert, unwired placeholder pill reserved in the toolbar ahead of v2 free-text search shipping - keeping the slot present now means the shell won't reflow layout once that feature lands.

nodes.label: Narrow-Viewport Filters Sidenav Collapse
nodes.rationale: Below the 960px breakpoint (same threshold app.ts already uses for the primary nav collapse) the inline facet controls and sort row collapse into a single 'Filters · N' trigger opening a full-height mat-sidenav with the same controls, while active-filter chips stay inline regardless of collapse state (dashboard-handoff.md §2/§3).

nodes.label: Centered Dialog Supersedes Right-Side Drawer
nodes.rationale: Design brief §09 originally called for a right-side drawer; superseded by a centered MatDialog per operator direction because the drawer's backdrop was scoped only to RepositoryGrid's own bounding box (not the full page) and couldn't be made to look like a centered modal without fighting mat-drawer's docked-edge slide animation. The score breakdown is shown always-expanded here (there's room) rather than tucked behind a 'Why this score?' panel as on the card.

nodes.label: Removed Standalone Views (Discovery Feed, Bookmarks, Trending)
nodes.rationale: Hidden Gems is now the dashboard's only repository-list view. Discovery Feed shared the same card-grid + filter-bar structure before removal as a standalone view; the dedicated Bookmarks view used the same FilterSortBar/RepositoryCard/RepositoryDetailPane/BookmarkToggle components before its removal; a standalone Trending tab was merged into Hidden Gems, which is why trendGrowth is now Hidden-Gems-specific. Each removal is tracked by its own changelog entry, referenced repeatedly across these shared components' header comments.
nodes.norm_label: removed standalone views (discovery feed, bookmarks, trending)
